gaps.sentence: We watched the orchestra ___ (REHEARSE) from the balcony.
Be careful not to ___ the medicine — read the label twice (USE).
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misuse means to use something incorrectly. A base verb follows 'not to'.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.

gaps.sentence: The trip gave us a lot of ___ (PLEASE).
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: pleasure (note the irregular spelling).
The prefix un- forms the negative adjective: unusual. An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: Their ___ was celebrated with a big party (MARRY).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'Their'; note the spelling change
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'marry' is 'marriage' (-age); an adjective cannot follow 'Their' as subject.

gaps.sentence: He ___ denied knowing anything about the plan (FIRM).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'denied': firmly. Note the doubled m before -ly.
